explanation: Graded number neuron: it fires strongly (0.55-1.0 of max) on a mid-sentence cardinal number, in digits or words, that a measuring frame introduces as an amount: after 'at', 'to', 'every', 'for', 'after', 'averaging', 'the first/next', or 'a/an' plus a hyphenated unit ('heated at [80]', 'every [5] minutes', 'sentenced to [twelve]', 'a [45]-minute', with the hyphen also strong). Any other mid-sentence number, a bare count ('bought 4 apples') or a label of a physical thing ('room 9', 'Version 4', 'extension 5512', 'Patient 12', 'bus 9', 'read chapter 9'), still gives weak activity of about 0.25-0.45 of max, so count it as weakly active; it is near zero for years ('in 1989', 'in 2010'), for document cross-references after 'see', 'in', 'turn to' or at sentence start ('See Figure 12', 'Table 3 lists', 'turn to page 47'), for a number right after the word 'number', and for non-number words (only 'at' after 'stored' reaches about 0.25 of max).
